case_title: Suresh & Anr. v. State of Haryana
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Cr.P.C. s.357 A
aggravating_circumstances: Failure to explain the facts in their exclusive knowledge, recovery of dead bodies and personal belongings at the instance of the accused
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment and other lesser sentences
neutral_facts: The prosecution case revolves around the kidnapping and murder of Devender Chopra and his son Abhishek Chopra. The deceased left their factory for their house in D.L.F., Gurgaon but did not reach their house. On 18th December, 2000, the deceased were kidnapped, and a ransom of fifty lacs was demanded. The family could not fulfill the ransom demand, and the kidnappers did not release the victims. The matter was reported to the police on 24th December, 2000. The police, with the help of the accused, recovered the dead bodies of the deceased and their personal belongings from covered gutters and other places. The post-mortem reports indicated that the deceased were killed by strangulation and cutting of the throat by a sharp weapon, and stab injuries in the chest and abdomen with a head injury caused by blunt force impact. The accused were apprehended at an STD booth, and their disclosure statements led to the recovery of the dead bodies and personal belongings. The trial court convicted the accused for kidnapping and murder, and the High Court affirmed the conviction.
